chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Hasan al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If you pray a part of the prayer during travel at a time other than its proper time, it does not harm."
For the intended meaning is the permissibility of delaying the prayer from its time due to an incident, excuse, or compulsion. As for advancing it, it is not permissible in any case.

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If one forgot facing the Qiblah or made a mistake in it, then remembered or recognized it while the prayer time was still remaining, he must repeat the prayer. And if the time had passed, there is no repetition for him, unless his prayer was due to forgetfulness and mistake in facing away from the Qiblah; in that case, he must repeat the prayer whether the time was still remaining or had passed.

key_terms.التَّأْخِير: Delaying prayer from its prescribed time

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating prayer if one realizes they faced the wrong Qiblah during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of delaying obligatory prayers during travel due to necessity (*‘udhr*), while clarifying that advancement (*taqdim*) is generally impermissible. It further refines the jurisprudence of *Qiblah* orientation, stipulating that a prayer performed with forgetfulness towards the wrong direction must be repeated regardless of whether the prayer time remains or has passed, a ruling derived from the principle of *Istishab* and the necessity of correct orientation for validity.
